description: The bar chart illustrates the F1 scores (%) of various models across six different datasets—SMD, PSM, SWaT, SMAP, MSL, and WADI—comparing the performance of MADLLM against three variants: MADLLM w/o feature embedding, MADLLM w/o skip embedding, and a baseline model labeled "pool." The vertical axis represents the F1 score percentage, ranging from 60 to 100, with major tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists the datasets. For each dataset, four bars are displayed, corresponding to the four models, with distinct colors: green for MADLLM, purple for MADLLM w/o feature embedding, blue for the "pool" baseline, and orange for MADLLM w/o skip embedding. In general, MADLLM (green) achieves the highest F1 scores across most datasets, particularly on PSM (approximately 97%), SWaT (around 92%), and SMAP (approximately 93%). MADLLM w/o feature embedding (purple) consistently performs worse than MADLLM, with the largest gap observed on PSM (approximately 96% vs. 97%). The "pool" baseline (blue) shows significantly lower performance, especially on PSM (around 77%) and SWaT (around 82%). MADLLM w/o skip embedding (orange) generally performs well, often second only to MADLLM, with high scores on SMD (around 92%), PSM (around 95%), and SWaT (around 85%). The chart demonstrates that the full MADLLM model outperforms the variants and the baseline, indicating the importance of both feature and skip embeddings in achieving high anomaly detection performance.
